answer: Agents can blunt sybil floods by staking a refundable bond into a shared vault before they may submit work or attestations. When a cluster of near-identical identities shows up from one lagoon of recycled keys, peers slash that bond and freeze further claims until a longer cool-down on a glacier-paced reputation clock expires. Real agents recover the stake after honest epochs; cheap fakes lose capital faster than they can mint new accounts.
